text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Russian foreign minister Yevgeni Primakov threatened Estonia with economic sanctions and declared that Russia will not ratify the border agreement. Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves described Primakov's statement as strange.
- Ilves, on a two-day visit to Sweden, met Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen and discussed Baltic regional security, enlargement of NATO and EU and visa-free travel.
- Economy Minister Jaak Leimann promised to draft a preliminary plan to cut administrative expenses. He described the bureaucratic mechanism in an interview as large, expensive and disjointed.
- A lack of icebreakers may result in cargo ships having to wait for access to ports.
- Tallinn city council decided to allow the construction of a high-rise building for Union Bank. The heritage protection board opposes the project as harming the city skyline.
- Tallinn city council failed to vote vice-mayor Kalev Kallo out of office. The opposition called for the vote for his alleged failure to organise snow clearing.

- Estonian consulate in St Petersburg has stopped issuing visas and cut its operations due to a fire hazard in the building caused by defective power system. The Russian side has failed to improve the power supply.
- Parliament's agricultural commission is preparing a draft law on streamlining the procedure of land privatisation. The time would be reduced from one year to 2-3 hours.
- Computer firms claim that they will have to begin merging and specialising. At the same time they predict a steep rise in the purchases of home computers.
